title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Corollary 3 (previous page). K is finitely generated over Q, with algebraic closure K̄. X and Y are geometrically connected K-schemes of finite type, and X is reduced. Y embeds, via a torsor, into an extension G of an abelian variety by a torus, i.e. Y sits inside a torsor under a semi-abelian variety. Each morphism f: X→Y induces a morphism of outer extensions π1(f): E_{X/K} → E_{Y/K} of Gal(K̄/K). Claim: if π1(f) = π1(g) up to π1(Ȳ)-conjugacy, then f = g. The previous page strengthens this: equality of the induced maps on the abelianized extensions (Gal by π1(X̄)^ab, resp. π1(Ȳ)^ab) already suffices.

This page first comments on that strengthening. Once 'arithmetic-geometric' hypotheses are in place, one can drop the anabelian (non-abelian π1) aspects and work only with abelian ones, but in an arithmetic setting. Corollary 1 α) used only the geometric hypothesis H1(f̄) = H1(ḡ): H1(X̄) → H1(Ȳ). Here the finer hypothesis is that, for every prime ℓ, f and g induce the same homomorphism of extensions of Gal(K̄/K) by H1(X̄,Z_ℓ) resp. H1(Ȳ,Z_ℓ). Geometrically, equality on H1 only gives f = g up to a translation. The arithmetic (Galois-extension) information is what kills that translation.

Proof of Cor. 3, as begun here:
(i) It suffices to show f(x) = g(x) for all x ∈ X(K). The hypothesis survives finite extension of K, every K̄-point is rational over a finite extension, and X is reduced, so its K̄-points are dense.
(ii) A rational point x gives a π1(X̄)-conjugacy class of sections s_x of E_{X/K} → Gal(K̄/K), and hence a class of sections of the abelianized extension.
(iii) The hypothesis implies that f(x) and g(x) give the same conjugacy class of sections of the abelianized extension for Y.

Completion, implicit and done on the next page via the maps (*) and (**). Write d = f(x) − g(x) ∈ G(K). The difference of the two section classes is the Kummer class of d in H^1(K, T̂(G)) = lim_n H^1(K, G[n]). So it remains to know that the Kummer map G(K) → H^1(K, T̂G) is injective for K finitely generated over Q. This holds because its kernel is the group of infinitely divisible elements of G(K), which is trivial: for the abelian part by Mordell–Weil–Lang–Néron, and for tori because ∩_n (L*)^n = 1 in finitely generated fields. Hence d = 0.

The problem this serves is the injectivity half of the section conjecture and the uniqueness half of the Hom conjecture. The next page states it as Theorem 3, for elementary Artin neighbourhoods ('variétés élémentaires d'Artin') whose geometric fibres are neither P^1 nor A^1.
errors: The previous page asks for conjugacy by an element of π1(Y); it should be π1(Ȳ). This is a minor slip.
Step (i) is quick but correct: passing to a finite extension L/K preserves the hypothesis (restrict to Gal(K̄/L)), and reducedness of X gives density of the K̄-points.

The reduction to the Kummer map is left implicit on this page. The essential arithmetic input (injectivity of G(K) → H^1(K, T̂G), from Mordell–Weil–Lang–Néron and its torus analogue) is not stated here.

The marginal note on the next page (K finitely generated over any prime field, X proper smooth) needs care in characteristic p. The prime-to-p Kummer map on A(K) can kill the p-primary torsion of A(K). So the p-part must be included, or a further argument given; the note itself is hedged.

ideas.what: Morphisms into (torsors under) semi-abelian varieties are determined by their action on the abelianized arithmetic fundamental extension, i.e. on Galois extensions by H1(X̄,Z_ℓ) for all ℓ.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity / uniqueness part of the Hom conjecture via the Kummer map and the (generalized) Albanese
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore following Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings; treated systematically e.g. in Stix's book on the section conjecture and in Nakamura/Tamagawa/Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: The letter to Faltings (1983) states the section and Hom conjectures and indicates that injectivity follows from Mordell–Weil; exact wording unsure.

ideas.what: A rational point gives a conjugacy class of sections of the fundamental extension, and the abelianized class is the Kummer class.
ideas.modern_name: Section map X(K) → S_{π1(X/K)} and abelian section map / Kummer map
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 27.6.1983; Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Methodological remark: once arithmetic-geometric input is available, drop the anabelian structure and argue with the abelian (H1) extension in an arithmetic setting. Geometric H1-equality fixes a map up to translation, and the Galois extension class fixes the translation.
ideas.modern_name: Abelian/metabelian reduction; Albanese plus Kummer argument

ideas.what: Theorem 3 (next page): the section map is studied for elementary Artin neighbourhoods with geometric fibres different from P^1 and A^1, i.e. allowing non-hyperbolic fibres such as G_m or elliptic curves, embedded in semi-abelian torsors.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the section map for Artin neighbourhoods / elementary anabelian varieties
ideas.where_published: Elementary anabelian varieties appear in the letter to Faltings and Esquisse; this precise hypothesis set is unsure.

missed.claim: This is a draft record of Grothendieck's own proof of the injectivity part of the section and Hom conjectures for maps into semi-abelian torsors. It explicitly reduces anabelian injectivity to ℓ-adic Kummer injectivity for all ℓ. The content is known and routine today, but this page documents how Grothendieck himself organized the argument (anabelian → abelian-arithmetic).
missed.quote: on peut laisser tomber les aspects anabéliens, pour jouer sur les aspects abéliens — mais dans un contexte arithmétique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows the injectivity half was regarded as 'easy' and handled via abelianization, consistent with the later literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the standard Albanese plus Kummer argument for injectivity; the page is historically illustrative but contains nothing absent from the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: The hypothesis of Cor. 1 α) should read 'H_1(f̄) = H_1(ḡ) : H_1(X̄) → H_1(Ȳ)', not 'H_1(Ȳ) = H_1(Ȳ)'.
The coefficients are probably 'H_1(X̄, Z_ℓ)' resp. 'H_1(Ȳ, Z_ℓ)', ℓ-adic integers; the hat is likely spurious or stands for completion.
Line 1 reads more like 'remontées par des hypothèses diverses [de nature] arithmético-géométriques' than 'hypothèses diophantiennes'.
In 'E_{X/K} sur E_{K̄/K}' the X was overwritten (originally X̄?), and the inserted phrase is 'conjugaison de scindages', replacing a struck 'd'...points'.
The insertion over 'quitte à' is 'faire une extension finie (du corps de base)'; 'cela rendra vrai' should probably read 'cela restera vrai'.
